lessons.title: The rise and fall of history's first empire

questions.q: What material did the Sumerians use to build their cities, since they had no stone or timber?
What invention did Sumerians create largely to help manage trade and record transactions?
What innovation let Sumerians farm successfully in a dry landscape?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, describe how Sumerians turned a resource-poor landscape into 'the cradle of civilization.' What single Sumerian invention do you think mattered most, and why?

lessons.title: How did they build the Great Pyramid of Giza?

questions.q: Who was the architect of the Great Pyramid?
About how many stones were used to build the Great Pyramid?
About how many years did the video say construction took?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, explain what organizing thousands of workers to build the Great Pyramid tells you about Egyptian government and society at the time.

lessons.subject: Social Studies
lessons.title: The secret behind how Chinese characters work

questions.q: What is the main subject of this video?
choices: The history and evolution of Chinese characters

questions.q: How does the video describe Chinese characters changing over time?
choices: They've stayed exactly the same for 5,000 years
They've evolved over thousands of years
They were borrowed entirely from another language

questions.q: A lasting writing system is an example of which characteristic of civilization?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, compare the role writing played in Sumer, Egypt, and China based on this week's three videos.

lessons.title: The five major world religions

questions.q: Which of these religions IS covered in this video?
How many major religions does this video cover?
The video describes these religions' histories as:

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, describe one way a religion discussed in the video shaped the civilization it grew up in (government, art, law, or daily life). Note: this video covers 5 of the 8 religions in our standard - ask a parent about Confucianism, Sikhism, and Taoism too.

lessons.title: The Importance Of The River Nile in Ancient Egypt

questions.q: What did the Nile provide to ancient Egypt, according to the video?
What did Egyptians regulate based on the Nile's waters?
Besides farming, what else did the Nile offer Egypt?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, explain how Egypt's geography (the Nile) shaped where and how its civilization grew.

lessons.subject: Social Studies
lessons.title: Ancient Mesopotamia Geography: The Fertile Crescent, Tigris & Euphrates Rivers

questions.q: What does "Mesopotamia" refer to, based on the video?
choices: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers

questions.q: What is the "Fertile Crescent"?
choices: A moon shape in the sky
A fertile farming region shaped like a crescent

questions.q: What technology did Sumerians and Akkadians use to farm successfully there?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, compare how the Tigris and Euphrates shaped Mesopotamian civilization to how the Nile shaped Egyptian civilization.

choices: How much of the sunlit Moon we can see from Earth

questions.q: What is a "New Moon"?
choices: The start of the lunar month, when the Moon isn't visible
A brand new moon that just formed

questions.q: About how long is a full cycle of moon phases?

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: What creates a total solar eclipse?

questions.q: What creates a total solar eclipse?
choices: The Moon passing between Earth and the Sun
The Earth passing between the Sun and Moon

questions.q: What has to line up for an eclipse to happen?
choices: Sun, Earth, and Moon in specific alignment

questions.q: The video mentions how civilizations throughout history reacted to eclipses. This reaction was often:

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: Reasons for the seasons

questions.q: What actually causes Earth's seasons?
choices: Earth's distance from the Sun changing a lot

questions.q: Why are seasons reversed in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
choices: Because of Earth's tilt relative to the Sun as it orbits

questions.q: Approximately what is Earth's axial tilt?

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, explain why summer and winter happen even though Earth's distance from the Sun barely changes.

lessons.title: How Inertia and Gravity work TOGETHER

questions.q: What two forces keep a planet in orbit rather than falling in or flying away?
What is inertia, based on the video?
choices: An object's tendency to keep moving in a straight line

questions.q: What would happen to a planet's straight-line inertia without gravity?
choices: It would fly off in a straight line

lessons.notebookPrompt: In 2-4 sentences, explain how gravity and inertia work together to keep a planet in orbit.

lessons.title: How far would you have to go to escape gravity?
